activity_c.text: Good morning, Nimal.
Today I want to talk about how you are handling safety procedures and maintenance work in the ICT lab.
How are things going?
Good morning, madam. Things are going well, but I think some of our system checks can be faster.
For example, the server-room inspection took longer than expected.
Why did it take longer?
Yesterday the backup server was slower than usual, and I had to restart the system twice.
The network layout was also more complicated than I thought.
I wasn’t expecting that.
I see.
When you check the servers today, what are you going to do first?
I’m going to inspect the cooling fans and test the UPS connection.
I must also record everything in the maintenance log, because the administration team needs clear reports.
Good.
You have to be systematic.
What about the new firewall unit?
Can you handle the configuration update?
Yes, I can, but the new firewall is more sensitive than the old one, so I have to be careful.
The old unit was slower, but it was easier than this new digital model.
Are you checking the PPE shelf regularly?
Yes, I am.
I check it every evening, but yesterday I wasn’t able to finish the anti-static wrist-strap testing.
I was too busy with the router-firmware repair.
You must not skip safety testing.
It is more important than small adjustments.
What happened with the router?
The status lights were brighter than normal, so I checked the firmware panel.
It was corrupted.
I reinstalled the software and reset the device.
Now it is working properly.
Good.
What are you doing about equipment inventory?
I am updating the cable and device register every day.
The new system is more accurate than the old notebook method, but it is also slower when the Wi-Fi drops.
That happens.
Do you think we need a backup system?
Yes, we can keep printed ICT safety checklists.
They are simpler than digital forms during busy hours.
That sounds practical.
Keep improving your methods.
It will make the whole lab more efficient than last month.
